title: Greeter survives a grace-time unlock; every later lock starts no greeter ("QProcess::start: Process is already running") and leaves a black screen with only a cursor
line: Locking the screen again after an unlock in grace time now always shows the lock screen, even if the old lock screen process got stuck.
explanation: An unlock within the grace time unlocks at once and only sends SIGTERM to the greeter. If that greeter doesn't exit (on the reporter's NVIDIA machine it ignored it), KSldApp keeps it in m_lockProcess, and the next lock calls QProcess::start() on a process that is still running, which only warns "Process is already running". The session is then locked with no greeter: a black screen with no password field. Now the grace-time unlock SIGKILLs the greeter if it is still running two seconds after the SIGTERM. If the screen is locked again before that, startLockProcess() kills the old greeter and starts the new one from its finished signal, so KWin never waits for it.

commits.message:
ksldapp: Kill a greeter that doesn't exit after a grace time unlock

An unlock in grace time only sends SIGTERM to the greeter. If it doesn't
exit, the next lock can't start a new greeter and leaves a black screen,
so kill it after two seconds, or right away when the screen locks again.

BUG: 528681

media.caption: Master: greeter stalled during a grace unlock, Lock 3 s later: session locked, no greeter, black screen (journal: "QProcess::start: Process is already running")
With the fix, same steps: the stuck greeter is killed 2 s after the unlock and the next lock shows the lock screen
Master: same black screen when locking again right after the grace unlock
With the fix, Lock 0.5 s after the grace unlock: the old greeter is killed at once and the new lock screen starts when it has exited

review.text: Escalating a grace-time unlock SIGTERM to SIGKILL after 2 seconds and deferring a new greeter launch via m_pendingLockProcess when the previous greeter is still exiting directly addresses the lockout root cause without blocking KWin. However, there is a state-machine bug in the new `logind::requestUnlock` + `m_pendingLockProcess` path: if a previous greeter killed by `startLockProcess()` was not a grace-time kill (e.g., relock immediately after password unlock) and logind unlocks before it finishes exiting, `finished(CrashExit)` will fall through to crash recovery and spawn a greeter while `m_lockState == Unlocked`. The 2 s timer in `unlock()` also captures `pid` without checking that the process is actually running.
changes: In the `m_lockProcess` `finished` handler, guard the crash-restart branch so it never restarts the greeter when `lockState() == Unlocked` (returning early and clearing `s_graceTimeKill`/`s_logindExit` if already unlocked).

In `KSldApp::unlock()`, only call `terminate()` and arm the kill timeout when `m_lockProcess->state() != QProcess::NotRunning` (and prefer a member `QTimer` stopped when `m_lockProcess` finishes, or at least guard `pid > 0`, so a timer with `pid == 0` is never scheduled).

reviews.text: KSldApp silently calling QProcess::start() on a still-running greeter is a real ksld defect that leaves a locked session with no greeter, and fixing it in ksldapp.cpp is the right layer whatever makes the greeter ignore SIGTERM. The SIGKILL after 2 s is guarded by a pid check. The deferred start is handled first in the finished handler, so the killed greeter isn't counted as a crash. Pending state is cleared by doUnlock, upgraded by an Immediate lock and respected by a logind unlock, and the workers die with the greeter through PDEATHSIG. The journal excerpts and the after screenshot match each path (timer kill, kill on relock, healthy greeter untouched). Follow-up worth noting in the MR: the greeter's SIGTERM handler calls QCoreApplication::exit(1), which does nothing if it runs before app.exec() (e.g. during initialViewSetup on a slow NVIDIA start). That is a likely greeter-side cause, but this fix makes ksld recover either way.
